source: MAFF / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), Royal Government of Cambodia — ខ្សែសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំស្វាយចន្ទីនៅកម្ពុជា (Cashew Value Chain Study in Cambodia), field survey report (250 household respondents across major cashew-growing provinces), 2017, 57pp
text:
Key recommendations from the 2017 MAFF cashew value chain study, based on its findings across cultivation, pest/disease, and market sections.

Strengthen farmer organization: form or strengthen farmer groups/cooperatives so growers can coordinate on quality standards, negotiate collectively with buyers, and access market information and technical extension more effectively than as individual sellers.

Support quality-based marketing and local processing: build farmer-group and district/provincial-level understanding of processing standards and quality control, so that some value-addition (rather than pure raw-material export to Vietnam) becomes feasible over time, and so producers are less dependent on a single raw-material export channel.

Invest in technical training for the M23 variety: because M23 is relatively new to many farmers, provide proper technical training on its management (pruning, fertilization, and especially pest/disease management), since farmers' limited experience with this variety was identified as a contributing factor in losses.

Prioritize urgent pest research: commission formal identification and control research for the 'mousetè' (Helopeltis tea mosquito bug) problem specifically, given its severity and the risk that continued unresolved damage could drive meaningful numbers of farmers to reduce area or abandon cashew altogether (see cashew_tea_mosquito_bug_helopeltis).

Address soil quality for new plantings: provide soil-improvement guidance for farmers establishing cashew on newly-cleared or poor-quality land, since soil quality problems were identified as a contributing factor to weak establishment and growth in new plantings.

Preserve traditional variety genetic diversity: as farmers shift toward the higher-value but more pest-susceptible M23 variety, the report flags a risk of losing traditional local Khmer cashew varieties, which showed better natural resistance to pests and diseases in side-by-side comparisons; maintaining some traditional variety plantings (or breeding/grafting work that combines local resistance with M23-type kernel quality) is suggested as a way to balance productivity with resilience.

Improve market transparency and linkages: work toward reducing farmers' exposure to opaque, broker-driven price swings — for example by improving farmers' access to price information and by exploring domestic processing or diversified export linkages beyond the single dominant Vietnam raw-material channel — to give producers more stable income and negotiating power.
caveat: Some specific figures in this source (percentages, price points, yield ranges) were transcribed from a scanned document at a resolution where certain digits were hard to confirm with full pixel-level certainty. Figures are reported as best-effort readings of the source; anyone using exact numbers for decisions should verify against the original report where possible.
